gap: No result ChatGPT got states which lithium pack and charger go with which cart: Club Car's Onward Lithium comes as a 4.0 kWh Base pack with a 650 W HF Li-Ion shelf charger (25–40 mi in year 1) or a 7.0 kWh XR pack with a 900 W charger (45–60 mi), and the lead-acid-to-lithium kits are sold by cart make (Vatrer's Club Car kit is listed for 48V DS, Precedent, Tempo and Onward; 36V carts need Vatrer's separate 36V kit).
standout_why: Pages compared: the cited clubcar.com/en-us/personal/golf-carts and the uncited onward-2-passenger page. Both say only that lithium is a powertrain option ('Lithium battery requires no upkeep') and give no kWh, charger or range per pack. The cited ttgolfcarts.com inventory page showed only empty filters and no listings when I opened it. ChatGPT's own answer said 'lithium pricing varies', and its generic table ('48V or 72V', '30–60 miles') doesn't tie anything to a model. ChatGPT asked whether the shopper wanted to upgrade an existing cart, but no result lists which kit fits which cart make or voltage. The Onward 2-passenger sell-sheet PDF (result 16, not cited) may hold the pack figures, but I could not extract its text, so I can't rule out that it states them.
decides: For a new cart, the Onward choice is really Base vs XR: the 4.0 kWh pack covers about the same year-1 range as a new lead-acid Onward (25–40 vs 30–50 mi), while XR's 7.0 kWh gives 45–60 mi. Lithium also unlocks the 7-inch display and dual wireless chargers. For an existing cart, the shopper should match the kit to cart make and voltage. The 48V Vatrer Club Car kit ($1,579.99) and the Redodo 48V kit ($1,149.99) each carry a 5.1–5.4 kWh pack and a 58.4V 18A charger, more energy than the Onward Base pack, at a fraction of the price of a new cart. 36V carts need the separate 36V Vatrer kit ($1,269.99). E-Z-GO ELiTE replacement packs are split by battery generation (Gen 1, 2017–2021; Gen 2, 2022+).
